findings.title: Dayjs objects compared via === always evaluate to false
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset,'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset,'minutes')` compares two distinct Dayjs object instances by reference, so it is always false regardless of whether start and end actually represent the same instant. This branch intended to detect zero-length overrides never triggers, so that special case is not handled as intended.

findings.title: workingHour end computed from start time (copy-paste bug)
findings.body: In the new working-hours check inside checkIfIsAvailable, both `start` and `end` are computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` — `end` should instead be based on `slotEndTime`. As written, `end` always equals `start`, so the `end > workingHour.endTime` check can never correctly flag a slot that starts within working hours but ends after them, causing slots that extend past working hours to incorrectly be treated as available.

findings.title: DST/offset adjustment uses override.start for both organizer and invitee offsets, applied uniformly to start and end
findings.body: The same `offset` (computed solely from `override.start`) is applied to both `override.start` and `override.end`. If the override spans a DST transition boundary in either the organizer's or invitee's timezone, using a single offset for both the start and end instants can produce incorrect start/end minutes, silently shifting or shrinking the override window by an hour in those edge cases. This is a narrow edge case but was not covered by any test (only non-DST-transition dates are exercised in the added test).

findings.title: New timezone test doesn't actually test a different organizer/invitee offset scenario thoroughly
findings.body: The new 'different timezone' test only changes the invitee timeZone between two zones that are both ahead of UTC (+5:30 and +6:00) and expects identical UTC output, which only confirms the override is stored/read in UTC-correct form; it does not cover timezones on opposite sides of UTC (e.g., negative offset) or a case where the organizer's and invitee's day boundaries diverge, which is exactly the scenario this PR claims to fix (slots not adjusting across different timezones for overrides near day boundaries).
